title: Meet Cabernet Sauvignon
subtitle: Structure and blackcurrant
objectives: Describe Cabernet Sauvignon's flavours and structure

steps.title: The king of structure
steps.body: Cabernet Sauvignon gives deep-coloured wines with blackcurrant, black cherry, cedar, mint and sometimes green pepper. It has high tannin and high acidity, so it ages well. It is the world's most planted wine grape, about 340,000 hectares, grown in almost every wine country.

steps.title: An accidental cross
steps.body: In 1996, DNA research at UC Davis showed that Cabernet Sauvignon is a natural cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc, probably in 17th century Bordeaux. Its small, thick-skinned berries, with a high ratio of skin and seed to juice, explain its colour and tannin. It also resists rot and frost well, since it buds late.

steps.prompt: Which two grapes are the parents of Cabernet Sauvignon?
steps.explanation: DNA testing in 1996 showed it was a cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for deep colour, a nose of blackcurrant with cedar, mint or pencil shavings, and a palate with firm tannin and fresh acidity. In cooler sites, a green pepper or leafy note. In warmer ones, ripe black fruit and sometimes eucalyptus. It often sits in oak, adding vanilla and toast.

steps.prompt: Cabernet Sauvignon buds late, which helps it avoid spring frost.
steps.explanation: Yes. Late budding protects it from frost, but late ripening means it needs a warm site.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet Sauvignon gives blackcurrant, cedar and firm tannin
It's a 17th century cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc
Small, thick-skinned berries give colour, tannin and ageing power
